Every state has an else self-loop covering irrelevant events, so no transitions are missed. The predicate-only event key_lost is used exactly as an event (one-step regression from u2 to u1 with -0.1), and since re-entering u1 requires has_door_key to progress again, regressions are explicit as required: dropping the key with the door closed sends the agent back to u1 (must re-acquire the key), and blocker_moved can regress only via u2's key_lost path, which is consistent with the task emphasis. Ordered transition coverage is complete: u0 handles both ball-first and key-first branches (key-first is safe because key_lost requires door_open false, and has_door_key implies not key_lost); u2 covers door_open and key_lost; u3 covers target_picked_up; u4 is absorbing. Reward safety holds: progress rewards (0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 1.0) are dense (each meaningful proposition change is rewarded) but bounded, and the only penalty (-0.1 for key_lost) is modest and task-aligned ('try not to drop the key while the door is still closed'). The machine correctly handles the interaction constraints: has_door_key and target_picked_up never co-occur, key_lost and has_door_key never co-occur (guarded by !key_lost on entry to u2), and key_lost requires door_open false, matching the definition. The task's soft constraint 'at any moment holding the key, try to have the door open then or open it later' is enforced structurally: key_lost while in u2 demotes to u1, requiring re-acquisition. Minor note: once in u1, dropping the ball again (blocker_moved regressing to false) is not modeled, since blocker_moved false is covered by the else self-loop; this is acceptable because the task does not demand re-blocking penalization, and u1's semantics (ball moved) remain correct.

feedback: `blocker_moved` is wrong. It scans the entire grid and checks for any ball whose left neighbor cell holds a door, i.e. it tests whether any cell directly left of a door contains a ball — not whether the cell in front of the door is ball-free. First, 'in front of the door' is not the cell to the door's left in general (door orientation varies), and the logic is inverted: it returns True when there is no such ball anywhere adjacent in that direction, which can be true even while the blocker ball still sits in front of the door (e.g. ball below/right of the door), and False in wrong cases. It must find the door's cell (dx, dy) by type scan and check that `env.grid.get(dx - 1, dy)` holds no ball, exactly as specified in the code notes. Everything else (`has_door_key`, `door_open`, `target_picked_up`, `key_lost`) matches the documented expressions and API scope.
